drug_class: Disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD) — oral gold compound
purpose: Auranofin is used to treat rheumatoid arthritis. It helps reduce joint pain, swelling, and stiffness. It is typically used when other treatments have not worked well enough.
how_it_works: Auranofin contains a tiny amount of gold, which helps calm down your immune system when it is overactive and attacking your own joints. By slowing down this immune reaction, it helps protect your joints from further damage. It works slowly over several months, so you may not notice improvement right away.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are diarrhea, loose stools, stomach upset, nausea, and rash. Some people also notice mouth sores or mild skin itching. Diarrhea is the most frequently reported problem, affecting many people who take this medication.
warnings: Auranofin can sometimes cause serious problems with your kidneys, liver, or blood cells, so your doctor will order regular blood and urine tests while you are on it. It can also suppress your bone marrow, making it harder for your body to fight infections. Tell your doctor right away if you notice unusual bruising, bleeding, fever, or changes in how much you urinate. Do not take this medication if you are pregnant, as it can harm the baby.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 3 mg taken by mouth twice a day, or 6 mg once a day. After several months, your doctor may increase the dose to 3 mg three times a day if needed. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes and do not stop without talking to your doctor first.
